summary.title: [Praktikum] Online Store V.2
summary.description:
SYSTEM OVERVIEW:
E-commerce platform utilizing multi-tier architecture with clear separation of concerns across three security zones (Internet, DMZ, Internal Network).

SECURITY ARCHITECTURE:
- API Gateway with rate limiting (100 req/minute per IP)
- JWT token-based authentication (ASVS 2.1.1)
- Password hashing with bcrypt (cost ≥12) (ASVS 2.4.1)
- PostgreSQL database with AES-256 encryption at rest
- Input validation on all endpoints (ASVS 5.1.3)
- Webhook signature verification (HMAC-SHA256)
- Comprehensive audit logging (ASVS 7.1.1)
- Session management via Session Store (Redis)

KEY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS:
SR-01: JWT token validation on all protected endpoints [ASVS 2.1.1]
SR-02: Password hashing with bcrypt cost minimum 12 [ASVS 2.4.1]
SR-03: Input validation and sanitization [ASVS 5.1.3]
SR-04: Audit logging for sensitive operations [ASVS 7.1.1]
SR-05: Rate limiting on API endpoints [ASVS 2.2.1]

TRUST BOUNDARIES:
- TB-01: Internet ↔ DMZ (Public internet access)
- TB-02: DMZ ↔ Internal Network (Backend services)

data.description: End-user accessing e-commerce platform via web browser

data.name:
Payment
Gateway
data.description: External payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) handling transaction processing

data.name:
API
Gateway
data.description: Entry point for all API requests. Handles rate limiting (100 req/min), request routing, and initial validation. Implemented with Kong/NGINX

threats.title: User Identity Spoofing via Missing Authentication
threats.description: Attacker sends requests without JWT token or with invalid token, attempting to access protected endpoints as unauthenticated user
threats.mitigation:
Enforce JWT Authentication on All Endpoints

Implement middleware that validates JWT signature and expiry on all protected endpoints. Return 401 Unauthorized for missing/invalid tokens.

threats.title: DoS Attack via Rate Limit Bypass
threats.description: Attacker bypasses rate limiting using distributed IPs, botnet, or header manipulation (X-Forwarded-For spoofing). Floods API Gateway with requests causing service unavailability
threats.mitigation:
Multi-Layer Rate Limiting with WAF

Implement rate limiting on multiple layers: 
(1) Per-IP limit (100 req/min), 
(2) Per-user limit (1000 req/hour), 
(3) Endpoint-specific limits, 
(4) Deploy Web Application Firewall (WAF) to detect/block botnet traffic

data.name:
Auth
Service
data.description: JWT token generation, validation, and session management. Issues tokens with 1-hour expiry. Stores active sessions in Session Store

threats.title: Weak Password Hashing Leading to Credential Compromise
threats.description: If passwords are hashed with weak algorithms or low iteration counts, attackers with database access can brute-force credentials offline using rainbow tables.
threats.mitigation:
Implement Bcrypt with Minimum Cost 12

Use bcrypt with cost parameter ≥12 for all password hashing. Bcrypt automatically handles salt and provides adaptive hashing

threats.title: JWT Token Claim Manipulation
threats.description: Attacker modifies JWT token claims (user_id, role, permissions) by forging or exploiting weak signature validation. Gains access to admin functions or other users' data.
threats.mitigation:
Strong JWT Signature Validation & Algorithm Enforcement

Always validate JWT signature using HS256/RS256 (reject 'none' algorithm). Verify expiry timestamp (1 hour max). Validate issuer and audience claims. Implement token refresh mechanism with separate refresh tokens. Never trust client-supplied tokens without verification

data.name:
Order
Service
data.description: Business logic for order creation, processing, and tracking. Validates orders, manages inventory, and initiates payment requests

threats.title: SQL Injection via Unvalidated Input
threats.description: Provide a description for this thrAttacker injects malicious SQL through order search, filtering, or customer name fields. Bypasses input validation and executes arbitrary SQL commands accessing unauthorized data or modifying database.eat
threats.mitigation:
Parameterized Queries & Input Validation

Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) for all database operations. Implement whitelist input validation on all user-facing endpoints. Sanitize all input before use. Use ORM frameworks (e.g., Sequelize, TypeORM) that handle parameterization.

data.name:
Payment
API
data.description: Wrapper for external payment gateway. Securely forwards payment requests, verifies webhook signatures (HMAC-SHA256), handles transaction responses

data.name: PostgreSQL Database
data.description: Primary database storing users, orders, inventory, and transaction history. Uses AES-256 encryption at rest. Located in Internal Network

threats.title: Sensitive Information Logged in Plain Text
threats.description: Error messages, query logs, or audit logs contain sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII) in plain text. Developer debugging or log analysis exposes secrets.
threats.mitigation:
Title	Structured Logging with PII Redaction

Implement structured logging framework. Redact PII in logs (mask email, truncate names). Log sensitive operations to audit trail with metadata (user_id, timestamp, operation).

data.name: Session Store
data.description: Redis cache for active session tokens. 1-hour TTL. Located in DMZ for quick access by Auth Service

data.name: User Login Request
data.description: HTTPS POST request with username/password. Port 443. Contains credentials

threats.title: Order Data Tampering in Transit
threats.description: Attacker intercepts HTTPS request and modifies order details (quantity, price, address) before reaching server. Man-in-the-Middle attack if HTTPS validation fails.
threats.mitigation:
Enforce TLS 1.3 with Certificate Pinning

Use TLS 1.3 minimum for all data flows. Implement certificate pinning on client-side. Validate HTTPS certificates. Add request signing with HMAC for sensitive payloads

data.name: Login Response
data.description: HTTPS response with JWT token. Set-Cookie header. HTTPOnly, Secure, SameSite flags

data.name: Order Request
data.description: HTTPS POST with JWT bearer token. Contains order details (items, quantity, address)

data.name: Create Order
data.description: Internal API call with JWT validation. Passes validated order details and user context.

data.name: Store Order
data.description: SQL INSERT query over encrypted connection (TLS 1.3). Stores order with encryption key

threats.title: Sensitive Data Exposure in Database
threats.description: Database breach exposes PII (names, addresses, phone numbers) and payment information if not encrypted. Attacker gains access to customer data and order history
threats.mitigation: Enable AES-256 encryption at rest for PostgreSQL. Encrypt PII fields (name, phone, email, SSN) with application-level encryption.

data.name: Initiate Payment
data.description: HTTPS request to Payment API wrapper with order_id, amount, customer info (encrypted)

data.name: JWT Token Response
data.description: JWT token with claims (user_id, expiry, permissions). Signed with HS256. 1-hour expiry

data.name: Webhook Callback
data.description: HTTPS POST with HMAC-SHA256 signature. Async notification of payment status. Signature verified before processing

threats.title: Webhook Signature Validation Bypass
threats.description: Attacker sends forged webhook notification to Payment API claiming payment success without valid signature.
threats.mitigation:
HMAC-SHA256 Webhook Signature Verification

Verify all webhook requests with HMAC-SHA256 signature. Compare signature from webhook header with server-side computed signature. Use strong webhook secret (256-bit key). Verify timestamp to prevent replay attacks. Implement webhook secret rotation annually.

data.name: Payment Request
data.description: HTTPS POST to external payment processor. API key in Authorization header. Includes encrypted payment details.

data.name: Auth Request
data.description: Internal API call to validate credentials. HTTP/gRPC. Includes hashed credentials
